environmental.acoustic-noise: 37.8 dBA AC AFO, 38.9 dBA AC AFI, 39.7 dBA DC AFO and DC AFI (datasheet Table 3, ISO 7779 at 23 C)
environmental.altitude: up to 3049 m operating (10,000 ft); 4877 m non-operating
environmental.humidity: 10 to 85 percent noncondensing operating; 0 to 95 percent non-operating
environmental.operating-temp: 0 to 45 C (32 to 113 F) for AFO models; 0 to 35 C for AFI models

features.macsec: IEEE 802.1AE on all Gigabit Ethernet and 10 Gigabit Ethernet ports
features.optics-qsfp: 40GbE QSFP+ SR (multimode) and DAC direct-attach copper (datasheet, Supported Optics)
features.uplink-module: one slot; 4-port 1/10 GbE SFP+ EX-UM-4X4SFP (not part of the shipping configuration)
features.virtual-chassis: up to 10 members; the four rear QSFP+ ports are Virtual Chassis ports by default

management.console: mini-USB on the front, RJ-45 CON2 on the rear
management.lcd: 2 lines of 16 characters with Menu and Enter buttons
management.oob: MGMT RJ-45 with link activity and status lamps (rear)
management.usb: one USB port on the rear

performance.airflow-cfm: fan 22 CFM, each power supply 7.5 CFM; 59 CFM total with two supplies (datasheet)
performance.throughput: 369 Mpps wire speed for the 48-port models (datasheet)

physical.depth-no-psu: 416.1 mm (16.38 in) with no power supply or uplink module (Table 10)
physical.depth-with-uplink: 457.3 mm (18 in, 45.73 cm) with a power supply and an uplink module (Table 10)
physical.weight: 13 lb (5.9 kg) with no power supply and no fan module; 16.1 lb (7.3 kg) with one power supply and two fan modules

power.psu-redundancy: N+0 or N+N; up to two supplies, one is enough for the chassis

configs.description: EX4300-48T as shipped - one 350 W AC power supply (AIR OUT) in slot 0 with a cover panel over slot 1, two EX4300-FAN (AIR OUT) fan modules, and the uplink slot covered. Front-to-back airflow.
configs.name: ac

configs.description: EX4300-48T-AFI - one 350 W AC power supply (AIR IN) in slot 0 and two EX4300-FAN-AFI (AIR IN) fan modules: back-to-front airflow, air entering at the rear and leaving through the front.
configs.name: afi

configs.description: EX4300-48T-DC - one 550 W DC power supply (AIR OUT) in slot 0 and two EX4300-FAN (AIR OUT) fan modules: front-to-back airflow, DC powered. The DC supply does not provide PoE.
configs.name: dc

configs.description: EX4300-48T-DC-AFI - one 550 W DC power supply (AIR IN) in slot 0 and two EX4300-FAN-AFI (AIR IN) fan modules: back-to-front airflow, DC powered.
configs.name: dc-afi

configs.description: EX4300-48T-S - the spare chassis, shipped with no power supply and no fan module; either AC or DC supplies and AIR OUT or AIR IN fans are ordered separately, and the datasheet's spare-chassis matrix says which combinations are supported. The supply and fan bays are shown open.
configs.name: s

gaps.wanted: Where the two-hole protective earthing terminal sits on the rear panel and its hole pitch. The guide's Table 69 puts it on the rear panel with a two-hole lug and 10-32 screws, and Figure 13's right-edge screws carry no callout. A rear photograph or a dimensioned drawing settles it.

A straight-on studio photograph of the rear, and of the DC and AIR IN supplies. The maker's image library holds none for this family, so the rear is read off the low-resolution callout figure and the supply and fan art follows the isometric drawings.

A straight-on studio photograph of the EX4300-48T front. The maker's library has the EX4300-48P and EX4300-24T; the 48T front is taken from the 48P, which the guide's shared figure shows to be the same face.
The bracket positions of the front-mounting brackets: no figure in the guide measures them, so no ear position or kit is listed.
A library component for an LCD display; the LCD panel is a decor rectangle until one exists.
The EX-UM-4X4SFP uplink module and its ports, left for the later uplink-module slice; the bay takes only the cover panel here.

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor
one of `power-max-w`, `power-max-ac-w`, `power-max-dc-w` in `attrs.power` (profile `networking` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices
`physical-context` on 5 bays (front 1, rear 4); `physical-context` on port group rj45 - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays

ac-psu-seating.note: The guide's AC power supply table (Table 30 and the text around it) lists 350 W, 715 W and 1100 W supplies for every EX4300 except the 48MP, so the bays accept all three AC ratings; this non-PoE model ships with the 350 W supply (Table 3 and Table 8; datasheet Table 1) and its power budget tables (Table 34) work the 715 W and 1100 W combinations for the PoE models. The 715 W and 1100 W supplies are seatable here but no configuration of this device ships them.

airflow.note: Guide Tables 7, 27, 28 and 31: AIR OUT (AFO) is front-to-back and AIR IN (AFI) is back-to-front. The guide's Table 3 and Table 28 list this model in four builds: EX4300-48T (AC, AFO), -AFI (AC, AFI), -DC (DC, AFO) and -DC-AFI (DC, AFI), which are configurations of this chassis because their rear differs only by the supplies and fan modules seated; -S is the spare chassis without them. AFI models run 0 to 35 C against 0 to 45 C for AFO (datasheet).

chassis.note: Guide Table 10 and the datasheet: height 1.72 in (4.37 cm) = 43.7 mm; width 17.36 in (44.1 cm) = 441.0 mm, "the outer edges of the front-mounting brackets extend the width to 19 in", so 441.0 is the body between the bracket flanges; depth 16.38 in (41.6 cm) with no power supply or uplink module, 17.51 in (44.47 cm) with a power supply installed and 18 in (45.73 cm) with a power supply and an uplink module. The modelled depth is 444.7 mm, the figure with the power supply fitted, as shipped; the other two are in attrs. The guide's centimetre figure for the last (45.73) is 0.1 mm from its inches (457.2): the centimetre figure is carried. 1RU.

colour.note: The face is the median of 400 pixels of bare plate between the ports and the LCD in the 24T studio photograph, #898d94. The supply and fan faces are a tone darker and their tone is taken from the community NetBox elevation (estimated); see the components.

ears.note: NOT MODELLED. The guide's inventory (Table 68) ships two mounting brackets and mounting screws and says the switch mounts in a two-post or four-post rack; the datasheet lists the kits EX-4PST-RMK (four-post), EX-RMK (rack-mount) and EX-WMK (wall-mount) as separate items. No figure measures the bracket position, so no ear position is written and no rail kit is listed in chassis.kits. The kit's part number is recorded here for the later dedupe.

front-ports.note: 48 jacks in two stacked rows, four blocks of six columns. The dark jack cavities of the top row read, in mm from the left edge, 14.13, 28.12, 42.10, 56.08, 70.06 and 84.04 in the first block and 102.89, 191.64 and 280.55 for the first column of the next three (the 24T photograph reads 14.33 and 103.08), so the column pitch is 13.98, the registry's 13.97 ganged-jack pitch (0.550 in), and the blocks start 88.8 mm apart, a 4.98 mm gutter. Row centres read 15.5 and 30.7 mm down on this photograph and 14.9 and 29.6 on the 24T one: the pooled 15.2 and 30.0 were the first draft, and the render laid over the photograph at matched scale sat 0.8 mm high, so the rows centre 16.0 and 30.8 mm down (a 14.8 step, which is also what the registry's ganged-jack notes allow for a 1U face; the registry's 12.09 is a magjack-only figure). The top row is the same part turned 180 so that its keyway is up, as the photograph shows lamp tabs above the upper jacks and below the lower.

front-right.note: Read off the 48P photograph at 3.29 px per mm with the face's left edge at 0 (the 24T photograph agrees within a millimetre): LCD window 377.2 to 412.8 x 6.8 to 16.4 mm (35.6 x 9.6); the EX4300 legend above it centred at 395.4, 4.1; Menu button centre (422.2, 9.0) and Enter button (422.2, 17.2), 6.1 mm across; three chassis status lamps at x 428.9, y 6.2, 9.9 and 13.6; a face screw each side of this block at (367.4, 12.8) and (436.0, 13.1); the mini-USB console jack at (359.7, 5.8) with CON1 printed to its left; the uplink slot opening 363.3 to 437.2 x 24.2 to 42.9 mm. Each is placed by eye on that photograph.

fru-bays.note: Two power supply bays (PSU 0, PSU 1) and two fan bays (0, 1), each seating the guide's FRU parts. Mixing AFO and AFI parts, or AC and DC, is forbidden by the guide and is left to the configuration: a bay lists every part it can take and a configuration seats a matching set. The cover panel the guide ships for an empty supply slot is seated in slot 1 as shipped. The guide says the plain EX4300-48T and the -AFI do not support DC supplies and that the -DC, -DC-AFI and -S models do; the DC supplies are seated in those configurations only. No supply or fan is built into the chassis: all are FRUs.

gate-1-front.note: THE FRONT PHOTOGRAPH PASSES. ex4300-48p-front-high.jpg shows the face 1452 px across (x 24 to 1475) and 144 px down: aspect 10.08 against the stated 441.0 / 43.7 = 10.09, so it is near-orthographic and carries geometry, at 3.29 px per mm. Positions are good to about half a millimetre. The 24T photograph (3.245 px per mm) gives the same column centres to 0.2 mm, the second image the pitch is measured against. The guide's Figure 5 covers the 48-port EX4300 front for the T and P models alike and is a perspective drawing that gives counts only. No photograph of the 48T itself exists in the maker's library, so its front is the 48P's: the guide shows one front for both, and the NetBox community elevations show the 24P and 24T faces identical.

gate-1-rear.note: THE REAR CALLOUT FIGURE PASSES. Guide Figure 13 (g022074) is a flat rear elevation: rendered at 600 dpi its chassis outline is 1950 x 194 px, aspect 10.05 against 10.09, 4.42 px per mm. Positions on the rear are fractions off it, good to about half a millimetre; it is a low-resolution raster.

interface-names.note: Not printed and not modelled. The guide's configuration examples name the 48-port switch's jacks ge-0/0/0 to ge-0/0/47 and the uplink module's ports ge-0/2/0 to ge-0/2/3 and xe-0/2/0 to xe-0/2/3. The built-in QSFP+ ports' names are stated nowhere held. No table gives the numbering rule, so the names stay out of the file as a block and go here.

lamp-legends.note: drawing-vs-photo, and the PHOTOGRAPH wins: the guide says the three chassis lamps are labeled ALM, SYS and MST, but both photographs show three bare lamps with no legend beside them. The CON1 legend, about the same height, resolves in the same photograph, so the silence is a reading and not the image's limit. No legend is drawn. The order top to bottom is the guide's order of naming (ALM, SYS, MST); no document states it, so it is estimated.

lcd.note: The LCD panel shows two lines of 16 characters (guide, LCD Panel in EX4300 Switches). It is drawn as the dark green window the photograph shows; no library component exists for a display and none is added, so it is a decor rectangle and not a part.

lifecycle.note: Searched Juniper's end-of-life notices and third-party trackers on 2026-10-21. Trackers list end-of-life notices for the EX4300-32F (last order 2026-03-31) and the EX4300-48MP (last order 2026-12-29) and for older bundle SKUs (2020), and none for the EX4300-24T, -24P, -48T or -48P; Juniper's own milestones page did not render for the search, so the absence is unconfirmed. Recorded as none-announced.

other-faces.note: No source draws the top, bottom or sides flat: the guide's front and rear figures show them in perspective with a logo on the lid and mounting holes in the sides. Each carries an `empty` sentence.

port-lamps.note: Guide, Network Port, Built-In QSFP+ Port, Uplink Port, and Uplink Module Port LEDs, Figure 30 and Tables 21 and 22: each 10/100/1000BASE-T port has two lamps, a Link activity lamp (green, blinking with activity, steady when linked) and a Status lamp whose meaning is chosen with the LCD Enter button (ADM, DPX or SPD on a non-PoE model). The lamps are the jack housing's two corner windows (common/rj45-ganged-eth) and carry that component's default vocabulary. Which window is which on this hardware is not stated by any document held, so the pairing is the component's convention.

port-numbering.note: The photograph prints the numbers in pairs under each column: 0 and 1 under the first column, 2 and 3 under the second, up to 46 and 47, with the even number set higher and the odd lower beside it. The even number belongs to the upper jack and the odd to the lower, so numbering runs down each column and then across. The guide's CLI interface names are not printed on the metal and are not modelled; the photograph prints no block legends.

power.note: Guide Table 34 (AC) and Table 49 (DC): the base power the system needs is 175 W for a 48-port switch; a single 350 W supply leaves 175 W for PoE on a PoE model, and this non-PoE model has no PoE. The 550 W DC supply is N+0 or N+N like the AC ones. No typical or maximum draw of the switch itself is stated by the guide or the datasheet.

rear.note: Guide Figure 13 (g022074), 4.42 px per mm, rear seen from behind with x = 0 at the left of the drawing: MGMT and CON2 jacks stacked at 9.7 to 25.5 mm (centres y 16.6 and 30.8), the ESD point at (36.2, 8.4), the vertical USB port at (35.1, 28.7), fan module 0 from 49.1 to 97.7, four QSFP+ ports from 108.0 to 183.5 on the registry's 19.0 mm pitch (the figure's separators read 107.9, 127.4, 146.8, 165.8 and 184.3), fan slot numbers beside the block, fan module 1 from 194.9 to 243.5, power supply slot 0 from 257.5 and slot 1 from 348.9 (module edges found in the 600 dpi figure at 257.3 and 348.7), each 84.0 mm wide, and a strip at the right edge. The serial number label (callout 4) sits at 101.3 to 123.2 x 13.6 to 18.1. The figure is shared by the 24-port and 48-port models, and the guide's DC note says the DC supplies are installed in the same slots.

rear-ground.note: The guide says the protective earthing terminal of the EX4300 is on the rear panel (Table 69: two-hole terminal, two 10-32 screws, Panduit LCD10-10A-L lug) but no figure identifies it or gives its pitch, and the rear-panel figure's right-edge screws are not named by a callout. It is not modelled; see gaps.

rear-qsfp-lamps.note: Guide Figure 13 callout 11 and Figure 32: each QSFP+ port has two lamps below it, a Link activity lamp and a Status lamp (Table 24: steady green when the 40-Gigabit port is up). Eight small rectangles below the block at y 39.6, each pair 7.4 mm apart about its port's centre. The lamps' roles within a pair are not stated.

sources.note: EX4300 Switch Hardware Guide, Juniper Networks, published 2025-08-12 (414 pages; https://www.juniper.net/documentation/us/en/hardware/ex4300/ex4300.pdf): Figures 5 and 7 (48-port panel drawings), Figures 11 and 13 (callouts), Table 3 and Table 8 (models and what each ships with), Table 10 (chassis size and weight), Tables 18 to 26 (LEDs), Tables 27, 28, 30, 31, 40-42, 47, 48 (fans and supplies), Table 34 and Table 49 (power budgets) and Table 68 (cover panels). EX4300 Line of Ethernet Switches Datasheet (https://www.juniper.net/content/dam/www/assets/datasheets/us/en/switches/ex4300-line-of-ethernet-switches-datasheet.pdf, 17 pages, PDF created 2022-07-25): Table 1 (models), Table 2 (spare chassis), Table 3 (acoustics), physical and environmental specifications, ordering information. Juniper's straight-on studio photographs ex4300-48p-front-high.jpg (1500 x 211 px, the PoE sibling, whose front is the same) and ex4300-24t-front-high.jpg (1500 x 195 px) from its image library. The NetBox device-type library's EX4300-24P, 24T and 48P elevations (community drawings, not the maker's) were used only to cross-check counts and which side a feature sits. The guide's own panel figures are isometric drawings, so every front position is read off a straight-on photograph and every rear position off the flat callout figure. The maker's image library has no EX4300-48T photograph: both addresses tried for it (ex4300-48t-front-high.jpg and ex4300-48t-rear-high.jpg, once each) returned an error page. Terms of use: the guide, datasheet and photographs are Juniper's, published for customers; none is copied into the library, only transcribed facts and new drawings.

uplink-slot.note: Every EX4300 24-port and 48-port switch has one front-panel uplink module slot (guide, Uplink Modules in EX4300 Switches); uplink modules are not part of the shipping configuration and the guide's inventory (Table 68) says a cover panel for the slot is provided. The slot is a bay that takes the cover panel here; the EX-UM-4X4SFP module it is sold with is left for a later slice. The photographs are of switches with a module fitted, so they give the opening and not the cover.
